description: Figure 3 is a horizontal bar chart that illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from the Whisper large-v3 model after applying a series of cumulative automated optimisation steps. The chart displays the effect of five distinct optimisation steps: "Normalised", "Add Spacing", "Remove Spacing", "Americanisms", and "Dates", which are listed on the vertical axis. The horizontal axis represents the "Difference in Average WER from Whisper large" in a linear scale ranging from 0.000 to 0.003. For each optimisation step, two bars are shown, representing the performance of the NESAC ft model (orange) and the SESHA ft model (green), as indicated by the legend. The bars are sorted in descending order of the difference in WER. The NESAC ft model consistently shows a higher WER difference than the SESHA ft model for all steps. The highest difference is observed for the "Add Spacing" step, with the NESAC ft model at approximately 0.00344 and the SESHA ft model at approximately 0.00344. The lowest difference is for the "Dates" step, with the NESAC ft model at approximately 0.00257 and the SESHA ft model at approximately 0.00228.
